title: perch
description: Solana validator watchtower: validators, checks, RPC endpoints, disks, peers and notifications. https://github.com/TheChimpions/perch-watchtower

list.name: datasource
list.label: Prometheus
list.description: The Prometheus that scrapes your perch instances.

list.name: job
list.label: Job
list.description: The Prometheus job your perch targets are scraped under. Found automatically.

list.name: cluster
list.label: Cluster
list.description: The Solana cluster each instance is pinned to with [watchtower] cluster.

panels.title: Instances up
panels.description: perch instances Prometheus could scrape, out of those that have ever reported.

panels.title: Checks firing
panels.description: Checks past their hold-down and alerting right now, across the selected instances.

panels.title: Validators delinquent
panels.description: Selected validators any endpoint reports as delinquent.

targets.expr: count(max by (validator) (perch_validator_delinquent{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", validator=~"$validator"}) == 1) or vector(0)

panels.title: Instances blind
panels.description: Instances that could not get enough answers from their RPC endpoints to evaluate checks. Blindness is reported on its own schedule; it never pages as a validator problem.

panels.title: In maintenance
panels.description: Instances with an active silence or maintenance window (perch maint).

panels.title: Lost notifications
panels.description: Alerts that failed every delivery retry during the selected time range. Anything above zero means someone was not told.

panels.title: Instances
panels.description: One row per perch instance. Cycle age climbing past a few minutes means that instance is wedged. Owner shows which instance sends alerts for its scope. Validator is the build its own local RPC reports.

panels.title: Checks not healthy (empty is good)
panels.description: Only the periods a check was unhealthy (red) or could not be evaluated (gray). Gray is time you were not actually being monitored for that check: usually an RPC outage, or a check still warming up.

panels.title: Hold-down progress
panels.description: How far each unhealthy check is toward firing: 100% is its hold-down (pending_for). A check that climbs repeatedly but never reaches 100% is a real condition the hold-down is keeping quiet.

targets.expr: ((perch_check_unhealthy_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} > 0) / on (instance, check) (perch_check_pending_for_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} > 0) * 100) * on (instance) group_left (name) perch_watchtower_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}

panels.title: Firing now
panels.description: Every check currently alerting, and how long it has been confirmed unhealthy.

targets.expr: (perch_check_unhealthy_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} and on (instance, check) (perch_check_firing{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} == 1)) * on (instance) group_left (name) perch_watchtower_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}

panels.title: Vote and root distance
panels.description: Slots between the cluster tip (the most advanced endpoint) and the validator's last vote and root. Dashed lines are the default alert limits: 200 for votes, 400 for roots.

targets.expr: max by (validator) (max by (instance) (perch_endpoint_slot{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) - on (instance) group_right perch_validator_last_vote_slot{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", validator=~"$validator"})

max by (validator) (max by (instance) (perch_endpoint_slot{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) - on (instance) group_right perch_validator_root_slot{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", validator=~"$validator"})

panels.title: Delinquent
panels.description: Whether any endpoint reported the validator delinquent. perch pages only when several independent endpoints agree, so a single red sliver here may not have paged.

panels.title: Vote credits per hour
panels.description: Credits earned per hour. A drop to zero while the validator is not delinquent is the voting-but-not-landing failure that vote_stalled pages for.

panels.title: Skip rate this epoch
panels.description: Leader slots that produced no block, as a percentage of slots assigned so far this epoch. Default limits: 20% notifies, 45% pages.

panels.title: Identity balance
panels.description: SOL in the identity account, which pays for votes. Default limits: below 3 SOL notifies, below 0.5 SOL pages.

panels.title: Leader slots this epoch
panels.description: Assigned leader slots and blocks produced so far this epoch.

defaults.noValue: No leader slots yet this epoch

panels.title: Alpenglow
panels.description: Whether Alpenglow is in force on this cluster. Once it is scheduled, the very next epoch boundary already checks every vote account.

panels.title: VAT per epoch
panels.description: The Validator Admission Ticket burned from every admitted vote account at each epoch boundary. It falls as slot times shorten.

panels.title: Vote accounts under the minimum
panels.description: Selected validators whose vote account holds less than rent-exempt plus one VAT. Under Alpenglow they will be excluded at the next boundary.

targets.expr: count(max by (validator) (perch_validator_vote_account_balance_sol{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", validator=~"$validator"}) < scalar(max(perch_vote_account_minimum_sol{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Missing BLS keys
panels.description: Selected validators whose vote account has no BLS public key. Under Alpenglow a vote account without one cannot vote or produce blocks.

targets.expr: count(max by (validator) (perch_validator_bls_registered{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", validator=~"$validator"}) == 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Vote account balance
panels.description: Each vote account against the balance it must hold at the next epoch boundary (dashed): rent-exempt plus one VAT. The VAT is burned at every boundary, so a vote account with no commission income steps down by one VAT per epoch.

panels.title: Vote accounts
panels.description: Balance, BLS key, and what the commission earned last epoch does against the VAT. Epochs left counts the boundaries the balance still passes at that rate; blank means the account earns more than the VAT and is not draining. Before Alpenglow is scheduled these are what would happen.

panels.title: Endpoint usable
panels.description: Whether each endpoint gave a usable answer each cycle. Red is noise perch absorbed: an endpoint that fails never pages on its own.

panels.title: Endpoint errors per minute
panels.description: Transient errors (timeouts, 429s, 5xx) are expected on free endpoints. Config errors (a bad key, a plan that does not cover the call) do not go away by themselves and quietly cost you quorum.

panels.title: Slots behind the most advanced endpoint
panels.description: An endpoint more than 300 slots behind (the default) has its answers discarded for that cycle, so a frozen endpoint cannot vote a broken validator healthy.

targets.expr: (max by (instance) (perch_endpoint_slot{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) - on (instance) group_right perch_endpoint_slot{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) * on (instance) group_left (name) perch_watchtower_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}

panels.title: Projected time to full
panels.description: perch's own least-squares projection, the exact value its alert tests. Absent means not filling, or not enough history yet. Default limits: under 24h notifies, under 6h pages.

defaults.noValue: Not filling, or under 45m of history

panels.title: Free space
panels.description: Space available to the validator on each monitored filesystem.

panels.title: Used and inodes
panels.description: Space and inodes in use. A filesystem can run out of inodes with space to spare; default inode limits are 85% and 95%.

panels.title: Read-only and scrape health
panels.description: A filesystem remounted read-only is how a disk usually fails under a validator; perch pages immediately. A failed node_exporter scrape freezes the disk checks rather than alerting.

panels.title: Cycle age
panels.description: Seconds since each instance last finished a cycle. It resets every interval; a line that keeps climbing is a wedged watchtower.

panels.title: Cycle duration
panels.description: How long each probe cycle took. Approaching the interval means endpoints are slow or timing out.

panels.title: Alerting owner
panels.description: Which instance is responsible for sending alerts. With alerting = "auto", exactly one instance of a redundant pair should be the owner at any moment.

panels.title: Peers, as each instance sees them
panels.description: Whether each instance can reach the peers it watches. A peer that is unreachable while its validator keeps voting is lost visibility, not an outage.

panels.title: Peer cycle age
panels.description: How long ago each peer completed a cycle, as reported by the instance watching it.

panels.title: Delivered in range
panels.description: Notifications each instance actually delivered during the selected time range, by channel. A restart resets perch's counters; increase() accounts for that.

targets.expr: (round(sum by (instance, channel) (increase(perch_notify_deliveries_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])))) * on (instance) group_left (name) perch_watchtower_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}

(round(sum by (instance, channel) (increase(perch_notify_failures_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])))) * on (instance) group_left (name) perch_watchtower_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}

panels.title: Notifications over time
panels.description: Deliveries per interval by instance and channel. Lost deliveries, in red, failed every retry.

targets.expr: (round(sum by (instance, channel) (increase(perch_notify_deliveries_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__interval]))) > 0) * on (instance) group_left (name) perch_watchtower_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}

(round(sum by (instance, channel) (increase(perch_notify_failures_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__interval]))) > 0) * on (instance) group_left (name) perch_watchtower_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}

panels.title: Time since the alert path was last proven
panels.description: Age of the last successful self-test per channel (perch test-notify, or the weekly scheduled one). The dashed line is two weeks: two missed weekly tests.

defaults.noValue: No self-test yet: run perch test-notify, or wait for the weekly one
